source_observation: The black material is a single connected, four-terminal shape inside a 4.7 um square. Each of the four straight ports expands into a rounded petal before narrowing into a compact central overlap; the image is mirror-symmetric about both axes.
topology_reasoning: This is a symmetric crossing rather than an MZI or directional coupler: the horizontal and vertical routes pass through the same central region and provide four optical ports. I model each route as two opposed primitive taper sections per arm, with a narrow straight access, a broad lobe, and a short taper back to a central square overlap. The union of the horizontal and vertical primitive assemblies creates the observed four-petal silhouette while preserving a clean, editable topology.
how_it_works: A waveguide entering any port traverses the rounded broadening into the central crossing and exits through the opposite port. The broad lobes provide a smooth transition into the central overlap; there are no resonant arms or separate coupling gaps visible in the binary footprint.

iterations.change_made: Initial four-arm taper/rectangle assembly; reference placement used an obsolete origin assignment and produced a collapsed 1.9 um square.

Replaced ignored reference origin assignments with GDSFactory 9.20.7 move() placement and corrected inward/outward arm orientations; the lobes matched the footprint but were still linear polygonal tapers.
Replaced the two linear taper polygons per lobe with a 25-point gf.Path plus variable-width cross-section: sinusoidal rise and cosine fall reproduce the rounded petal edges.
Increased the four access-port length from 0.52 um to 0.57 um so the deterministic GDS bbox exactly spans the calibrated 4.7 um footprint.
Adjusted the live lobe width profile to sin(t)^0.75 on the rise and cos(t)^1.2 on the fall, matching the measured early bulge and inner taper curvature.
Removed an unintended default WG cross-section added by the helper constructor; using gf.CrossSection(sections=(section,)) leaves only the intended layer-(1,0) variable-width Path geometry.
